subject: Islamic Studies
q: The year in which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was born is known as:
explanation: He was born in the year Abraha marched on Makkah with elephants, hence Aam-ul-Feel, the Year of the Elephant.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Abraha, who marched on the Ka’bah with elephants, was the ruler of:
explanation: Abraha governed Yemen on behalf of the Christian king of Abyssinia and led the elephant army against Makkah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Aminah, the mother of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), belonged to the clan of:
explanation: Aminah bint Wahb was from Banu Zuhrah, a clan of the Quraysh.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Aminah passed away on the way back from Yathrib at a place called:
explanation: She died at Abwa, between Madinah and Makkah, when the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was about six years old.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: After the death of his mother, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was brought up by his:
explanation: His grandfather Abdul Muttalib took charge of him; on Abdul Muttalib’s death the guardianship passed to Abu Talib.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: On the death of Abdul Muttalib, the guardianship of the young Prophet (PBUH) passed to:
explanation: Abdul Muttalib entrusted him to Abu Talib, the full brother of the Prophet’s father Abdullah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Haleema (RA), the foster mother of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), belonged to:
explanation: Haleema Sa’diyah was from the Banu Saad bin Bakr, a desert tribe known for pure Arabic, with whom he spent his early childhood.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Before Hazrat Haleema, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was briefly nursed by:
explanation: Thuwaybah, a freed slave-woman of Abu Lahab, nursed him for a few days before he was given to Haleema.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The incident of Shaq-e-Sadr (opening of the chest) in the Holy Prophet’s childhood took place while he was living with:
explanation: The first opening of the chest by angels is reported while he was a child in the care of Haleema among the Banu Saad.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: To which country did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) make his first trade journey?
explanation: As a boy he accompanied his uncle Abu Talib with a trading caravan to Syria (Sham).

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Christian monk who recognised signs of prophethood in the young Muhammad (PBUH) during the Syrian journey was:
explanation: Bahira, a monk at Busra, saw the signs in the boy and advised Abu Talib to protect him.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hilf-ul-Fuzul, in which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) took part before prophethood, was a pact to:
o: Rebuild the walls of the Ka’bah
Help the oppressed and secure justice
explanation: Hilf-ul-Fuzul was an alliance of Makkan clans pledging to support anyone wronged in Makkah, and the Prophet later praised it.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Harb-ul-Fijar (the Sacrilegious War) got its name because it was fought:
explanation: It was called “Fijar” (sacrilege) because the fighting between Quraysh–Kinanah and Qays violated the sacred months.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Who accompanied the Holy Prophet (PBUH) on the trade journey he made for Hazrat Khadijah (RA)?
explanation: Khadijah’s servant Maysarah travelled with him to Syria and reported his honesty, which led to her marriage proposal.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Before prophethood, the people of Makkah called the Holy Prophet (PBUH):
explanation: His honesty and trustworthiness earned him the titles Al-Amin (the trustworthy) and As-Sadiq (the truthful).

subject: Islamic Studies
q: During the rebuilding of the Ka’bah, the dispute over placing the Hajr-e-Aswad was settled when the Holy Prophet (PBUH):
o: Placed it on a cloth lifted by all the clan chiefs
Placed it himself without consulting anyone
Referred the matter to Abu Talib
explanation: He spread a cloth, put the stone on it, had a chief of every clan lift it, then set it in place himself, averting bloodshed.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In his youth, besides trade, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) earned his living as a:
explanation: He grazed goats for the people of Makkah, an occupation he said every prophet had followed.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The well of Zamzam, long buried, was rediscovered and dug again by:
explanation: The Prophet’s grandfather Abdul Muttalib re-excavated Zamzam, which gave his family the honour of supplying water to pilgrims.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) belonged to which clan of the Quraysh?
explanation: He was from Banu Hashim, named after his great-grandfather Hashim bin Abd Manaf.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was called “Abul Qasim” after his:
explanation: Qasim was his first son, born of Khadijah (RA), so his kunyah became Abul Qasim.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The first wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was:
explanation: He married Khadijah bint Khuwailid before prophethood and married no one else during her lifetime.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The period of Arabian history before the advent of Islam is called:
explanation: Jahiliyyah (ignorance) is the Islamic term for the pre-Islamic age, marked by idolatry and tribal injustice.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Cave of Hira, where the first revelation came, is situated on:
explanation: Hira lies near the top of Jabal-un-Noor (the Mountain of Light) on the outskirts of Makkah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: At what age was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) given prophethood?
explanation: The first revelation came in 610 CE when he was forty years old.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: After the first revelation, Hazrat Khadijah (RA) took the Holy Prophet (PBUH) to her cousin:
explanation: Waraqa, a learned Christian, recognised the angel as the one who had come to Musa (AS) and foretold his people’s opposition.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The period of secret preaching at the start of the Prophet’s mission lasted about:
explanation: For roughly three years Islam was preached privately before the command to proclaim it openly.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Among children, the first to accept Islam was:
explanation: Ali bin Abi Talib, then a boy living in the Prophet’s household, was the first child to embrace Islam.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Among freed slaves, the first to accept Islam was:
explanation: Zaid bin Harithah, freed and adopted by the Prophet, was the first of the freed slaves to believe.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In the early Makkan period, Dar-e-Arqam served as:
o: The council house of the Quraysh
A trading post of Hazrat Khadijah
A centre for teaching Islam and meeting believers
explanation: The house of Arqam bin Abi Arqam near Safa was where the early Muslims met and learned in secret.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) first publicly called the Quraysh to Islam from:
explanation: After the command to warn his kinsmen, he climbed Safa and addressed the clans of Quraysh.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Da’wat-e-Zul-Asheerah refers to the Holy Prophet’s invitation to:
o: His close relatives of Banu Abdul Muttalib
explanation: On the command “warn your nearest kinsmen”, he gathered the Banu Abdul Muttalib at a meal and invited them to Islam.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The real name of Abu Lahab was:
explanation: Abu Lahab, the Prophet’s uncle and bitter opponent, was named Abdul Uzza bin Abdul Muttalib.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Before Islam, Abu Jahl was known among the Quraysh as:
explanation: Amr bin Hisham was respected as Abul Hakam (father of wisdom); his hostility to Islam earned him the name Abu Jahl.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Who was sent by the Quraysh to offer the Holy Prophet (PBUH) wealth, leadership and kingship to give up his mission?
explanation: Utbah bin Rabi’ah made the offer; the Prophet replied by reciting the opening of Surah Ha-Mim As-Sajdah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Holy Prophet’s famous reply “even if they place the sun in my right hand and the moon in my left” was made to:
explanation: When the Quraysh pressed Abu Talib to restrain him, the Prophet told his uncle he would not abandon his mission for anything.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The first martyr in Islam was:
explanation: Sumayyah bint Khayyat, mother of Ammar bin Yasir, was killed by Abu Jahl for refusing to renounce Islam.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Bilal (RA) was tortured on the burning sands of Makkah by his master:
explanation: Umayyah bin Khalaf placed a rock on Bilal’s chest in the heat, yet Bilal kept repeating “Ahad, Ahad”.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Who purchased and freed Hazrat Bilal (RA)?
explanation: Abu Bakr bought Bilal from Umayyah bin Khalaf and freed him, as he did several other persecuted slaves.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Companion was made to lie on burning coals by the Quraysh for accepting Islam?
explanation: Khabbab bin Arat, an early convert without tribal protection, was tortured on burning coals.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The first migration of Muslims to Abyssinia took place in the:
explanation: Persecution drove a small group of Muslims to Abyssinia in the fifth year of prophethood.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Christian king of Abyssinia who gave refuge to the Muslim emigrants was:
explanation: The Najashi (Negus) of Abyssinia, known for his justice, protected the Muslims and refused to hand them over to Quraysh.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Who spoke on behalf of the Muslims in the court of the Najashi?
explanation: Jafar bin Abi Talib explained the teachings of Islam to the Najashi, who then refused the Quraysh demand.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In the court of the Najashi, Hazrat Jafar (RA) recited verses from Surah:
explanation: He recited the opening of Surah Maryam about Yahya and Isa (AS), which moved the Najashi to tears.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Quraysh sent which envoy to the Najashi to demand the return of the Muslim emigrants?
explanation: Amr bin al-As, then not yet a Muslim, led the embassy with gifts, but the Najashi refused to surrender the Muslims.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Umar (RA) accepted Islam after hearing the Qur’an recited at the house of his:
explanation: Umar went to his sister’s house in anger, heard verses of Surah Ta-Ha, and was moved to accept Islam.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Hamza (RA) accepted Islam on learning that the Holy Prophet (PBUH) had been insulted by:
explanation: Hamza struck Abu Jahl with his bow for abusing the Prophet and declared his own acceptance of Islam.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: For how long did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) and his clan remain besieged in Shi’ab-e-Abi Talib?
explanation: The Quraysh social and economic boycott confined Banu Hashim to the valley for about three years.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Quraysh document declaring the boycott of Banu Hashim was hung in:
explanation: The pact was hung inside the Ka’bah to give it sanctity; it was later found eaten by termites except for the name of Allah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Aam-ul-Huzn (the Year of Sorrow) is the year in which:
o: Abu Talib and Hazrat Khadijah (RA) died
explanation: In the tenth year of prophethood the Prophet lost both his protector Abu Talib and his wife Khadijah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Who accompanied the Holy Prophet (PBUH) on his journey to Taif?
explanation: Zaid bin Harithah went with him and was injured shielding him from the stones thrown by the people of Taif.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: At Taif, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) invited the chiefs of the tribe of:
explanation: Taif was the home of Banu Thaqif, whose leaders rejected him and set the street boys on him.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Addas, the Christian servant who offered grapes to the Holy Prophet (PBUH) at Taif, came from:
explanation: Addas was from Nineveh, the town of Prophet Yunus (AS), and accepted Islam after hearing the Prophet speak of Yunus.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: When the angel of the mountains offered to crush the people of Taif, the Holy Prophet (PBUH):
o: Asked for them to be punished
Hoped their descendants would worship Allah
Asked for a delay of one year
explanation: He declined, hoping that Allah would bring from them people who would worship Him alone, an example of his mercy.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: On returning from Taif, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) re-entered Makkah under the protection of:
explanation: Mut’im bin Adi, a non-Muslim chief, granted him protection so that he could return to Makkah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: On the way back from Taif, a group of jinn listened to the Holy Prophet’s recitation at:
explanation: At Nakhlah a company of jinn heard the Qur’an and believed, an event referred to in Surah Al-Jinn and Al-Ahqaf.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The night journey from Masjid-ul-Haram to Masjid-ul-Aqsa is called:
explanation: Isra is the night journey to Jerusalem; the ascent from there to the heavens is called Mi’raj.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The heavenly mount on which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) travelled on the night of Isra was called:
explanation: Buraq was the heavenly steed; Qaswa was the Prophet’s she-camel used on the Hijrah and in later journeys.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The five daily prayers were made obligatory on the occasion of:
explanation: The five daily prayers were prescribed during the Mi’raj, before the migration to Madinah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) is said to have earned the title “As-Siddiq” for:
o: Confirming the Isra and Mi’raj without hesitation
explanation: When the Quraysh mocked the account of the night journey, Abu Bakr at once affirmed it, and was called As-Siddiq.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Pledges of Aqabah were made by people who came from:
explanation: Groups from the Aws and Khazraj of Yathrib pledged allegiance at Aqabah near Mina, preparing the way for the Hijrah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: After the first Pledge of Aqabah, who was sent to Yathrib to teach Islam?
explanation: Mus’ab bin Umair became the first envoy and teacher of Islam in Yathrib, and many accepted Islam through him.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Second Pledge of Aqabah differed from the first mainly because it included a promise to:
o: Protect and defend the Holy Prophet (PBUH)
explanation: At the second pledge the Madinans undertook to defend the Prophet as they would their own families, which made the Hijrah possible.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Quraysh met to plot the killing of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) at:
explanation: Dar-un-Nadwah was the Quraysh council house where they agreed that men from every clan would strike him together.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: On the night of the Hijrah, who slept in the Holy Prophet’s bed?
explanation: Ali slept in his bed to mislead the besiegers and stayed behind to return the trusts people had left with the Prophet.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: During the Hijrah, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) took shelter in the Cave of:
explanation: They hid for three nights in the Cave of Thaur, south of Makkah, while the Quraysh searched for them.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The guide hired to lead the Holy Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) to Madinah was:
explanation: Abdullah bin Uraiqit, a skilled guide who was not yet Muslim, was trusted to take them by an unusual coastal route.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: During the Hijrah, who grazed goats near the Cave of Thaur to cover the tracks and supply milk?
explanation: Amir bin Fuhairah, Abu Bakr’s freed slave, grazed his flock over their tracks and brought them milk.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Who pursued the Holy Prophet (PBUH) during the Hijrah and was promised the bracelets of Kisra?
explanation: Suraqa’s horse repeatedly stumbled; he sought pardon and was promised Kisra’s bracelets, which he received in Umar’s caliphate.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: During the Hijrah, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) stopped at the tent of Umm Ma’bad, who is remembered for her:
o: Gift of a camel for the journey
Hosting him for a month in Quba
explanation: Umm Ma’bad’s vivid description of the Prophet to her husband is one of the best-known accounts of his features.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Hijrah of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) to Madinah took place in:
explanation: The migration took place in 622 CE, the year later adopted as the start of the Islamic calendar.
